label: input y at original position 3-4
explanation: Fires whenever the input token is y during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase at positions t=3 or t=4. On dev it fires on every such step (precision 1.0) and these steps hold 99% of activation mass. A weak tail (about 7% of active steps, low magnitude) comes from y at t=2 and t=5. It never fires on y at t=0-1 or t>=6, on any other token, or in the delimiter or copy phase, including when y is copied back as input. Magnitude: y at t=3 activates more strongly (all top examples, ~0.9) than y at t=4 (~0.6-0.7, the lower quartiles). Activation is somewhat lower when y is a repeat (in_first=0). Preceding tokens and L have little effect.

issues: No systematic counterexample found. On test, precision is 1.0 (0 false positives out of 30220 predicted steps), recall is 0.928 and mass recall is 0.992. The 2353 missed steps hold 0.8% of the activation mass and are all tiny (about 0.04-0.09 of max) activations on y at t=2 or t=5.
The weak tail at t=2/5 is sparse: (phase==0)&y&t in {2,5} has precision 0.085 and mass recall 0.008. Widening the predicate to t in 2..5 drops F1 to 0.72, so the original predicate is the better one.

The claim that it never fires in the copy phase checks out: y as input in phase 2 has precision 0. The profile also shows zero activation in the delimiter or copy phase, at t<=1 or t>=6, and on any token other than y.

Magnitude claims check out. y at t=3 has 0.93 coverage of the top activation quartile and only 0.04 of the bottom quartile. The low quartiles are mostly t=4. Repeats (in_first=0) are spread evenly across quartiles at about 0.11, so 'somewhat lower when repeat' is a weak claim at best but harmless.
Minor wording point: the label says 'original position 3-4', which correctly implies the pre-<DEL> phase. It does not overclaim relative to the predicate.
